# End-of-Year HR Checklist: How to Prepare Your Business for 2027


- Oluwakemi Adesina


- November 27, 2026


Table of Contents


Toggle


December is one of the busiest month in most Nigerian businesses. Payroll, bonuses, the end-of-year push, then the break.


An end-of-year HR review is a few days of sorting out your records, contracts and policies before the new year starts. Do it in December and January is calmer for the business.


You will not finish everything, so start with what costs you money when it is wrong: employee records and compliance. A late appraisal annoys someone. A missing contract or an unpaid pension remittance can cost you a lot more.


Also:


· Employee details never updated after a promotion, a name change or a move.


· Contracts agreed verbally and never signed, or signed and never filed.


· Appraisals half-done in June and quietly abandoned.


· Leave balances nobody reconciled, so nobody knows what the company owes.


· Grievances “handled” in a corridor and never documented.


None of these looks serious on its own. Together they are why January turns into catching up on your own records.


# **What an end-of-year HR audit is**


An HR audit is a structured review of your policies, processes, records and practices. The point is to find where your records and your reality are not aligned and fix them.


##


**HR compliance audit**


Whether your practices and documentation line up with the obligations that apply to you, which depend on workforce size, locations and what your people do. Run it against current official guidance, not last year’s notes.


##


**Employee records audit**


Whether your files are accurate and complete: job titles that match what people do, start dates that match contracts, contracts filed where you can find them. It sounds like filing, but it is the foundation of next year’s decisions.


##


**HR process review**


How the day-to-day work runs: recruitment, onboarding, leave, performance, offboarding. If onboarding ends with a signed contract in an email draft, no audit of the files will fix that.


# **End-of-year HR checklist for Nigerian businesses**


Here is the review we would actually run, roughly in order.


##


**1. Review and update employee records**


Pull every active file and check it against reality: contact and emergency details, job titles, start dates, reporting lines, contract, salary and benefits. We have lost count of how often a “Head of Sales” is still recorded as a sales executive. Our[guide to employee records management in Nigeria](https://blog.myeazipay.com/2026/08/31/employee-records-management-nigeria/) covers what a complete file should hold.


##


**2. Review employment contracts and documentation**


Check that everyone has a documented contract, that job descriptions match what people do now, that promotions were recorded rather than agreed in a meeting, and that fixed-term agreements are reviewed before they lapse. The common failure is the informal promotion: a bigger role and a new salary, but a contract nobody updated, so two years later both sides rely on different versions of the truth.


##


**3. Review and update HR policies**


Check the policies your team actually lives by: attendance, leave, remote and hybrid working, code of conduct, disciplinary and grievance procedures, data protection, health and safety, and benefits. A remote work policy written for a fully in-office team, still applied two years into hybrid work, is a set of rules nobody follows and a standard nobody can enforce.


##


**4. Complete employee performance reviews**


Close out the year’s appraisals: review objectives against what was achieved, document outcomes, capture feedback, and agree 2027 objectives. A review is only defensible if it rests on expectations set earlier and documented outcomes, not a manager’s memory in December.


##


**5. Review employee leave and attendance records**


Reconcile[leave](https://blog.myeazipay.com/2026/09/17/employee-leave-management-nigeria/) taken and outstanding, sick leave, unapproved absences and the year’s[attendance](https://blog.myeazipay.com/2026/10/07/employee-attendance-management-nigeria/) record, and confirm your public holiday arrangements. When approvals live in WhatsApp and memory, nobody can say what is owed, so someone is short-changed and nobody notices.


##


**6. Review employee training and development**


Look at what training actually happened against what was planned, where the skills gaps are, and which capabilities the business will need in 2027, then build next year’s calendar from that. Reviewing training against the business plan is what turns a budget into capability.


##


**7. Review employee benefits and welfare**


Check health insurance, pension-related employee information, allowances and welfare initiatives, whether all of it was documented and communicated, and whether it is still relevant and affordable. Benefits drift in two directions: promised informally and never documented, or inherited from another era and kept out of habit. Our[guide to employee benefits in Nigeria](https://blog.myeazipay.com/2026/09/07/employee-benefits-in-nigeria-a-complete-guide-for-employers/) sets out what is mandatory and what is a choice.


##


**8. Review recruitment and employee turnover**


Pull the numbers: how many you hired and lost, what recruitment cost, how long vacancies took to fill, and why people left where you know. Identify the critical roles that would hurt if the person walked. This is the section most businesses skip because it feels like reporting; it is the most useful one for next year’s budget.


##


**9. Review employee grievances and workplace issues**


Go through unresolved complaints, disciplinary cases and workplace conflicts, and confirm issues were documented, handled confidentially, and resolved through a fair process. An unresolved grievance does not disappear, it waits, and your best protection in any dispute is a documented, fair process that was actually followed.


##


**10. Review HR compliance requirements**


Map the obligations that actually apply to you and check your records against them: employment documentation, labour requirements, health and safety, pension responsibilities, data protection, and the tax and statutory records you must keep. Run this against current guidance, not last year’s understanding.


# **HR compliance requirements Nigerian businesses should check before 2027**


Confirm which obligations actually apply to you and check your records against them. Requirements differ by workforce size, sector and who you employ, so map what applies to you.


##


**Employment documentation and the Labour Act**


The[Labour Act](https://iclg.com/practice-areas/employment-and-labour-laws-and-regulations/nigeria/) (Cap. L1, LFN 2004) is Nigeria’s principal employment statute and sets minimum standards a contract cannot go below. It governs “workers” in the manual and clerical sense, while professional and managerial staff are bound mainly by their contracts and case law, one more reason a written contract matters.


On pay, the statutory national minimum wage is ₦70,000 per month under the National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Act 2024,[assented on 29 July 2024](https://statehouse.gov.ng/labour-leaders-praise-president-tinubu-over-approval-of-n70000-minimum-wage-and-promise-review-after-three-years/) , with the next review due around 2027. It covers the private sector, but it[does not apply to establishments with fewer than 25 workers](https://pavestoneslegal.com/the-national-minimum-wage-amendment-act-2024-key-updates-and-practical-tips-for-employers-in-nigeria/) .


##


**Pension: the seven-day window**


Every employer must contribute at least 18% of each employee’s monthly emoluments, split 10% employer and 8% employee, and remit both into the employee’s Retirement Savings Account **within 7 working days of paying salaries** . Late remittance carries a penalty of at least 2% of the unpaid contributions, and Section 103 of the Pension Reform Act 2014 carries fines or imprisonment ([PenCom FAQ, 2023](https://www.pencom.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/FREQUENTLY-ASK-QUESTION-2023-Final.pdf) ). Contributions are due for every worker on the payroll, not only permanent staff. Our[pension contribution calculator](https://www.myeazipay.com/resources/pension-calculator) shows the split your payroll should be producing.


##


**Workplace injury cover**


Under the Employees’ Compensation Act 2010, every employer contributes 1% of total monthly payroll to the Employees’ Compensation Scheme, funded entirely by the employer.[Deducting any of it from staff pay is an offence](https://nsitf.gov.ng/services) . Employers must register with NSITF, and the scheme covers people from their first day, including contract and casual staff.


##


**Employee data protection**


If you hold employee records, you are processing personal data under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. That means documenting a lawful basis, honouring rights such as access, correction and erasure, and[notifying the Commission of a breach likely to affect people’s rights within 72 hours](https://ndpc.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/NDP-ACT-GAID-2025-MARCH-20TH.pdf) . Businesses processing data on more than 200 people in six months fall into the “major importance” category, with[registration and annual audit duties](https://ndpc.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Updated-Guidance-Notice-on-Registtration-2024.pdf) .


##


**Payroll tax and statutory records: what changed for 2026**


The[Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025](https://tat.gov.ng/Nigeria-Tax-Act-2025.pdf) took effect on 1 January 2026, and employer obligations moved with them. PAYE now runs on six bands from 0% to 25%; the old Consolidated Relief Allowance is replaced by a Rent Relief of 20% of annual rent, capped at ₦500,000; NHF deductions are now voluntary for private-sector employees; and gratuity is taxable (see[DLA Piper’s summary](https://knowledge.dlapiper.com/dlapiperknowledge/globalemploymentlatestdevelopments/2026/payroll-taxes-and-employer-liability-closing-the-compliance-gap-under-nigerias-new-tax-regime) ). Reconcile PAYE against the 2025 Acts, not the law they replaced.


Not every obligation applies to every business, and the above is not legal advice. What applies depends on your workforce, sector and locations. Check it against current official guidance, and where a duty is unclear, confirm it with a qualified person before you act.


Not sure how well your business is managing payroll and compliance? Complete[Eazipay’s free payroll and compliance assessment](https://www.myeazipay.com/resources/business-assessment) to review your processes and spot the areas that may need attention.


# **HR policies Nigerian businesses should review before 2027**


You do not need to rewrite every policy every year. Revisit the ones where something actually changed: your workforce size, your locations, how people work, how you handle technology and employee data, and any change in the rules that apply to you.


A team that doubled in size needs a disciplinary process that scales past a corridor conversation. Adapt it to your business:


**HR policy** **What HR should review**


Leave policy Eligibility, approvals and leave records


Attendance policy Working hours, absence and reporting


Remote work policy Availability, communication and responsibilities


Disciplinary policy Procedures and documentation


Grievance policy Reporting and resolution processes


Data protection policy Employee information access and security


Health and safety policy Workplace risks and employee responsibilities


When you update a policy, date it, record who approved it, and tell staff. A policy nobody was told about is hard to rely on and easy to dispute.


# **How to prepare your HR department for 2027**


An audit that ends in a folder is a wasted audit. Turn what you found into a short, owned plan: prioritise the urgent documentation gaps, put a name against each action, set deadlines for policy updates, and put a recurring review in the calendar.


Owners and dates make the difference: “Review contracts” means nothing; “Chidi, all fixed-term contracts reconciled by 31 January” means something. And connect it to the business, which is why it is worth reading our[workforce planning guide for 2027](https://www.myeazipay.com/workforce) before you set next year’s training and hiring priorities.

# **How HR software can help businesses stay organised**


Software does not run the audit and it does not make you compliant on its own but it removes the excuse that nobody can find anything: when records and statutory remittances live in one place, reconciling leave becomes twenty minutes, and the review actually gets done.


[Eazipay](https://www.myeazipay.com/) is one platform built for this. It runs payroll, files PAYE, and remits pensions, NHF, NSITF and ITF automatically, keeps employee and workforce records in one place, and includes an audit readiness view.


# **Final end-of-year HR checklist for 2027**


Work down this page with a name and a date against each line.


· ☐ Update employee records


· ☐ Review employment contracts


· ☐ Update job descriptions


· ☐ Review HR policies


· ☐ Complete annual performance reviews


· ☐ Reconcile leave and attendance records


· ☐ Review training and development requirements


· ☐ Evaluate employee benefits


· ☐ Analyse recruitment and employee turnover


· ☐ Review unresolved employee grievances


· ☐ Check applicable employment compliance requirements


· ☐ Set HR priorities for 2027


· ☐ Assign responsibilities and deadlines
